learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">A torque of 30 N-m is acting on a wheel of mass 5 kg and moment of inertia 2 kg-m<sup>2<\/sup>. If wheel starts rotating from rest
then its angular displacement in 10 seconds will be-<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"

A. Question Explanation:

We're given a wheel with a known mass and moment of inertia. A torque is applied to the wheel, causing it to rotate from rest. We need to determine the angular displacement of the wheel after a specific time.

B. Given Data:

  • Torque (τ) = 30 N-m

  • Mass of the wheel: 5 kg (This information might not be directly used in the calculation)

  • Moment of Inertia (I) = 2 kg-m²

  • Time (t) = 10 seconds

  • Initial angular velocity (ω0) = 0 rad/s (since the wheel starts from rest)

C. Concept:

  • Newton's Second Law for Rotational Motion: This law states that the net torque acting on an object is equal to the product of its moment of inertia and its angular acceleration (τ = Iα).  

  • Rotational Kinematics: We'll use the equation of rotational motion that relates angular displacement, initial angular velocity, angular acceleration, and time:
    θ = ω0t + (1/2)αt².

D. Calculation:

  1. Calculate Angular Acceleration (α):

    • Using Newton's Second Law for Rotational Motion: τ = Iα ⇒ α = τ / I
      ⇒ α = 30 N-m / 2 kg-m² ⇒ α = 15 rad/s²

  2. Calculate Angular Displacement (θ):

    • Using the rotational kinematics equation: θ = ω0t + (1/2)αt²
      ⇒ θ = (0 rad/s)(10 s) + (1/2)(15 rad/s²)(10 s)²
      ⇒ θ = 0 + (1/2)(15 rad/s²)(100 s²)
      θ = 750 radians

E. Final Answer:

The angular displacement of the wheel in 10 seconds is 750 radians. Option (1)

"

1. Octet Rule: The octet rule states that atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to achieve a full valence shell of eight electrons.
2. CIF3 (Chlorine Trifluoride):

Explanation

  • This is a strong acid (HCl) and strong base (NaOH) neutralization reaction.
Given Data
  • HCl: 400 mL, 0.1 M
  • NaOH: 100 mL, 0.2 M
Concept
  • We need to find the excess of either H+ or OH- ions after the reaction.
  • Then, we'll calculate the pH based on the remaining ion concentration.
Calculation
  1. Moles of HCl: (400 mL / 1000 mL/L) × 0.1 mol/L = 0.04 moles
  2. Moles of NaOH: (100 mL / 1000 mL/L) × 0.2 mol/L = 0.02 moles
  3. Neutralization: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O
  4. Excess HCl: 0.04 moles - 0.02 moles = 0.02 moles
  5. Total Volume: 400 mL + 100 mL = 500 mL = 0.5 L
  6. [H+]: 0.02 moles / 0.5 L = 0.04 M
  7. pH: -log[H+] = -log(0.04) ≈ 1.4

The pH of the mixture is approximately 1.4.
Answer option 4, (1.4)

"

  • Homo neanderthalensis: Neanderthals are a close relative of modern humans but represent a more recent branch in human evolution.

It's important to note that Dryopithecus is often considered an even earlier ancestor than Ramapithecus, but it's not an option here. If it were, Dryopithecus would be the most primitive. Among the choices given, Ramapithecus is the most primitive.

options.text: Brain controls all reflexes and movements of the body
Sub-oesophageal ganglion supplies nerves to mandibles, maxillae, and labium
Ventral nerve cord is single and non-segmented
Abdominal ganglia are absent in adult cockroach

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which statement about the nervous system of cockroach is correct?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Brain (supra-oesophageal ganglia) is mainly sensory, while motor control and reflexes are governed by segmental ganglia, especially the sub-oesophageal one.<\/div>\n"

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">The gizzard of cockroach is adapted for:<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">The gizzard (proventriculus) has chitinous plates and bristles to grind food thoroughly.<\/div>\n"

qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which one is true for cockroach heart?<\/div>\n"

options.text: It is a 13-chambered dorsal tubular heart with
It is located dorsally and circulate blood in closed vessel
It is located ventrally and circulates haemolymph in closed vessels
It contains haemoglobin that transports oxygen

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which one is true for cockroach heart?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Cockroach has an open circulatory system, and its heart is a long muscular tube with 13 chambers, each having paired ostia.<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Phallomeres are chitinous and asymmetrical structures that play a crucial role in spermatophore transfer.<\/div>\n"

qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During jumping, frogs need sudden oxygen supply to muscles. Which structural adaptation ensures this efficiency?<\/div>\n"

options.text: Lymph hearts pump blood directly into arteries during vigorous movement.
Large surface area of cutaneous skin capillaries rapidly sends oxygenated blood to systemic arches.
Well-developed hindlimb muscles are richly supplied with blood from dorsal aorta branching arteries.
Buccopharyngeal cavity acts as a direct oxygen reservoir for leg muscles.

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During jumping
frogs need sudden oxygen supply to muscles. Which structural adaptation ensures this efficiency?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Jumping needs perfusion; hindlimb muscles richly supplied via branches of dorsal aorta. Lymph hearts move lymph (not arterial blood).<\/div>\n"

qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following statements about male frog is correct?<\/div>\n"

options.text: Ureters carry only urine and open into urinary bladder, while vasa efferentia open separately into cloaca.
Ureters serve as urinogenital ducts, carrying both urine and sperm, and open into cloaca.
Sperms travel from testes - ureters - cloaca, bypassing kidneys.
Oviducts and fat bodies also connect to cloaca in male frogs.

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following statements about male frog is correct?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">ln male frog the ureters act as urinogenital ducts, carrying urine+ sperm to the cloaca.<\/div>\n"

qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During active feeding in frog, venous blood returning from stomach and intestine first passes through:<\/div>\n"

options.text: Hepatic portal vein → liver → sinus venosus → right atrium
Directly into truncus arteriosus → systemic arches → liver
Hepatic artery → liver → pulmonary veins → left atrium

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During active feeding in frog
venous blood returning from stomach and intestine first passes through:<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Gut venous blood → hepatic portal vein → liver → sinus venosus → right atrium<br \/>\n(portal circulation).<\/div>\n"

qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During prolonged diving in frog (underwater stay), which of the following events occur simultaneously to maintain survival?<\/div>\n"

options.text: Fat bodies supply oxygen directly to gonads, and hepatic portal vein bypasses the liver to prevent oxygen loss.

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">During prolonged diving in frog (underwater stay)
which of the following events occur simultaneously to maintain survival?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"
Primary mode of gas exchange underwater - cutaneous respiration.
Frogs can absorb 02 through the skin when submerged. The skin is thin, vascularised and
kept moist, allowing diffusion of gases. During prolonged diving cutaneous respiration
increases to meet oxygen demand.
